name: Sri Lankan Mango Curry
steps: Wash firm green mangoes and cut around each stone into thick wedges, keeping the peel on to help them hold their shape. Do not use soft ripe mangoes.
Heat coconut oil in a deep pan. Crackle mustard seeds, then add onion and curry leaves for 5 minutes. Stir in garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add curry powder, turmeric and chilli with a splash of water and fry 1 minute. Add mango wedges, 180 ml water, sugar and salt, then cover and simmer 8–10 minutes until the mango begins to soften.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes until the mango is tender but not collapsing and the sauce coats a spoon. Stir gently to avoid breaking the wedges.
Taste for sour-sweet balance, adding a little more sugar only if the mango is very tart. Rest 5 minutes and serve with rice and a mild dhal.
tips: Choose hard green mangoes; their acidity is the defining flavour, while a small amount of sugar rounds off excessive tartness.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
